title: Unique Identifier Exposure
description: The Homeowner (EE1) provides a unique identifier (e.g., email, phone number, or unique ID) to the Home Hub (P1) for account registration. This identifier is unique globally or locally, allowing the Hub to link the data to the specific individual. If this identifier is not protected or is exposed in transit, it enables the Hub to identify the data subject.
assumptions: The identifier provided by the homeowner is unique and identifiable.

title: Processing of Identified Information
description: The Home Hub (P1) processes the homeowner's account registration data, which includes the unique identifier provided by EE1. This processing involves requesting and handling the identified information, which can be used to identify the data subject.
assumptions: The data collected during registration is considered identified information.

title: Pseudonym/Identifier Exposure
description: The Home Hub (P1) may store or process the unique identifier provided by EE1. This data contains a unique reference to the identity of the data subject, constituting identifiable information. If this identifier is not pseudonymized or is exposed, it allows the Hub to directly identify the homeowner.
assumptions: The identifier stored or processed by the Hub is used to identify the data subject.

title: Observed Communications
description: The interaction between EE1 and P1 involves data being transmitted (observed communications). The Home Hub (P1) observes the data flow from EE1, which includes the unique identifier and other personal data. This observation allows the Hub to detect the data subject's actions and data characteristics.
assumptions: The data flow is observed by the Home Hub.

title: Data Type Sensitivity
description: The Home Hub (P1) may collect and process sensitive data types (e.g., full name, address, phone number) from the homeowner. According to Dd.1.1, more sensitive data types are collected than functionally required, which increases the risk of privacy breaches if these sensitive attributes are exposed.
assumptions: The data collected includes sensitive attributes beyond what is strictly necessary for the registration process.

title: Excessive Volume
description: The Home Hub (P1) may process an excessive amount of personal data from the homeowner. This includes not only the unique identifier but also potentially other personal data (e.g., full name, address, email) that is collected and processed, potentially exceeding the functional requirements of the system.
assumptions: The data volume collected and processed by the Hub is excessive compared to what is functionally needed for the registration.

title: Unnecessary Processing
description: The Home Hub (P1) may perform unnecessary processing on the homeowner's data. This includes treating, analyzing, or enriching the data in ways that are not necessary to achieve the functional goals of the system (e.g., storing the full name or address for future reference beyond the registration).
assumptions: The data is further processed or stored in a way that is not strictly required for the registration.

title: Involved Parties
description: The Home Hub (P1) may make the homeowner's personal data accessible to a predetermined set of parties. This includes the Home Hub itself and potentially other services or systems that are known and anticipated at design time, amplifying the potential risk of data exposure.
assumptions: The data is shared with a static and fixed set of parties.

title: Unawareness of Processing
description: The Homeowner (EE1) may be unaware that their personal data (including the unique identifier and other personal data) is being collected, processed, stored, or disclosed by the Home Hub (P1). This lack of awareness is a significant privacy risk.
assumptions: The homeowner is not aware of the data collection and processing activities.

title: Lack of Data Subject Control
description: The Homeowner (EE1) may lack control over how their personal data is processed. This includes the lack of control to set preferences or consent regarding the collection, storage, and use of their data by the Home Hub.
assumptions: The homeowner cannot influence how their data is processed.

title: Invalid Consent
description: The Home Hub (P1) may process the homeowner's personal data without valid consent. This could occur if the consent obtained is invalid, not informed, or not legally sufficient, leading to unlawful processing.
assumptions: The consent obtained for the registration may be invalid or insufficient.

title: Linking via Unique Identifier
description: Guest User (EE2) provides a temporary access code to Home Hub (P1). This code is a unique identifier that can be used to link the Guest User to the Home Hub, enabling the Home Hub to identify and process the Guest User's data.
assumptions: The access code is unique and globally or locally unique within the system.

title: Processing of Identified Information
description: The Home Hub (P1) processes the access code provided by the Guest User (EE2). This code is identified information, as it is requested and processed by the system.
assumptions: The access code is identified information.

title: Identifiable Information via Identifier
description: The access code provided by the Guest User (EE2) is identifiable information. It contains a unique reference to the identity of the data subject (the Guest User), allowing the Home Hub (P1) to derive the identity of the Guest User from the code.
assumptions: The access code is identifiable information.

title: Observed Communications
description: The Guest User (EE2) communicates with the Home Hub (P1) by transmitting the access code. This communication is observed by the Home Hub (P1) and can be detected.
assumptions: The communication is observed by the Home Hub.

title: Data Type Sensitivity
description: The access code provided by the Guest User (EE2) is a sensitive data type. Depending on the context, this code may be perceived as highly sensitive and should only be collected and processed when strictly required.
assumptions: The access code is sensitive data.

title: Excessive Amount of Personal Data
description: The Guest User (EE2) provides a temporary access code, which is a form of personal data. This amount of personal data is processed by the Home Hub (P1) beyond what is functionally needed for the system's operation.
assumptions: The access code is personal data.

title: Unnecessary Processing
description: The Guest User (EE2) provides a temporary access code, which is processed by the Home Hub (P1) for the purpose of unlocking the front door. This processing is not necessary to achieve the functional goals of the system (unlocking the door).
assumptions: The access code is processed for the purpose of unlocking the door.

title: Unawareness of Processing
description: The Guest User (EE2) may be unaware that their access code is being collected, processed, and stored by the Home Hub (P1).
assumptions: The Guest User may not be aware of the processing of their access code.

title: Lack of Data Subject Control
description: The Guest User (EE2) may lack control over how their access code is processed by the Home Hub (P1).
assumptions: The Guest User may lack control over the processing of their access code.

title: Invalid Consent
description: The Guest User (EE2) may provide consent for the processing of their access code, but this consent may be invalid or insufficient, leading to non-compliance with privacy regulations.
assumptions: The Guest User's consent may be invalid or insufficient.

title: Linking via Unique Identifier
description: The Home Hub (P1) uploads camera clips to Cloud Video Storage (DS2) using a unique identifier (e.g., camera ID, file hash, or timestamp). This allows DS2 to link the data to a specific source, enabling identification of the data subject if the identifier is associated with personal data.
assumptions: The camera clips contain personal data (e.g., video content, metadata) that can be linked to a specific individual via the unique identifier.

title: Processing of Identified Information
description: The Home Hub (P1) processes identified information (e.g., camera ID, file hash, or timestamp) to upload the clips to Cloud Video Storage (DS2). This processing step directly involves handling data that is already identified or can be used to identify the data subject.
assumptions: The camera clips contain identifiable information (e.g., metadata, timestamps) that is processed by P1.

title: Observed Communications
description: The Home Hub (P1) uploads recorded camera clips to Cloud Video Storage (DS2). The act of uploading constitutes observed communications, which can be detected by DS2 or other systems monitoring the flow.
assumptions: The system or DS2 may detect the upload activity as observed communications.

title: Data Type Sensitivity
description: The Home Hub (P1) uploads camera clips to Cloud Video Storage (DS2). Camera clips may contain highly sensitive personal data (e.g., video content, metadata) that is collected and processed beyond what is strictly functionally required for the system's operation.
assumptions: Camera clips contain personal data that is more sensitive than functionally needed for the video storage system.

title: Excessive Volume
description: The Home Hub (P1) uploads recorded camera clips to Cloud Video Storage (DS2). The volume of personal data (the clips themselves) is processed and stored in excess of what is functionally needed for the system's operation.
assumptions: The system requires more personal data than is functionally necessary for video storage.

title: Propagation
description: The Home Hub (P1) uploads recorded camera clips to Cloud Video Storage (DS2). The data is propagated to a third-party service (DS2) where it is not needed for the Home Hub's primary functionality.
assumptions: DS2 is a third-party service that receives the data for storage purposes.

title: GDPR Noncompliance
description: The Home Hub (P1) uploads personal data (camera clips) to Cloud Video Storage (DS2) without explicit, valid consent from the data subjects. This may violate the principle of lawfulness in GDPR.
assumptions: The data subjects did not provide valid consent for the processing of their personal data by P1.

title: Linking via Unique Identifier
description: The Home Hub forwards a real-time motion alert to the mobile app backend using a unique identifier (e.g., user ID, device ID, or motion event ID). This allows the backend to link the alert to a specific individual or device, enabling tracking and profiling.
assumptions: The identifier used is unique within the system or across the context boundary.

title: Processing of Identified Information
description: The Home Hub processes identified information (e.g., user ID, device ID) to forward the motion alert. This processing enables the system to identify the data subject associated with the alert.
assumptions: The identifier used is unique and identifiable.

title: Linking via Identifier
description: The Home Hub forwards the motion alert using a unique identifier (e.g., user ID, device ID). This allows the mobile app backend to link the alert to a specific data subject.
assumptions: The identifier is unique and sufficient for identification.

title: Revealing Attributes
description: The motion alert contains revealing attributes (e.g., specific motion details, timestamp, location) that support the identification of the data subject when combined with the identifier.
assumptions: The alert includes enough attributes to uniquely identify the user.

title: Observed Communications
description: The Home Hub forwards a real-time motion alert as observed communication. This allows the mobile app backend to detect the alert's presence and content.
assumptions: The alert is transmitted as a message or signal.

title: Data Type Sensitivity
description: The motion alert may contain highly sensitive data types (e.g., location, biometric motion data) that are collected and processed beyond what is strictly functionally required for the alert delivery.
assumptions: The alert includes sensitive data types not strictly necessary for the core functionality.

title: Excessive Amount
description: The Home Hub forwards a real-time motion alert, which may involve an excessive amount of personal data (e.g., detailed motion logs, timestamps, location history) beyond what is functionally needed for the alert.
assumptions: The alert includes more data than strictly required for the alert.

title: Unnecessary Processing
description: The Home Hub forwards the motion alert, which may involve unnecessary processing and treatment of personal data (e.g., detailed motion analysis, enrichment, transformation) beyond what is needed for the alert.
assumptions: The alert includes data that is further treated or analyzed in ways not strictly necessary for the alert.

title: Propagation
description: The motion alert is propagated to the mobile app backend, which may be a separate service where the alert is not needed, leading to unnecessary data exposure.
assumptions: The backend service is a distinct entity where the alert is not required.

title: Involved Parties
description: The motion alert is made accessible to the mobile app backend, which may be a predetermined set of parties (e.g., a specific service or application) that is not functionally necessary for the alert.
assumptions: The backend is a known, static, and targeted service.

title: Unawareness of Processing
description: The data subject (user) may not be aware that their motion alert is being forwarded to the mobile app backend, focusing on the collection, processing, storage, or disclosure of their personal data.
assumptions: The user is unaware of the specific forwarding action.

title: Lack of Preferences
description: The data subject may lack control over how their personal data (motion alert) is processed, as they may not be able to set preferences or consent to the specific forwarding action.
assumptions: The user cannot customize or opt-out of the alert forwarding.

title: Invalid Consent
description: The motion alert may be processed without valid consent, as the user may not have explicitly consented to the forwarding of their motion alert to the mobile app backend.
assumptions: Consent is not explicitly obtained for this specific action.

title: Violation of Storage Limitation
description: The motion alert may be stored longer than functionally needed, as it is forwarded to the mobile app backend which may retain it for future use or analysis.
assumptions: The backend retains the alert beyond the immediate alert delivery.

title: Sensitive Data Collection
description: Motion-detected notifications are classified as highly sensitive personal data, which is collected and processed without strict functional necessity.

title: Granular Data Disclosure
description: Motion-detected notifications are disclosed with a high level of granularity, revealing specific details about the user's activity.

title: Excessive Processing
description: Motion-detected notifications are processed and stored for a duration longer than functionally required.

title: Excessive Exposure
description: Motion-detected notifications are broadcasted to a broad set of external parties (homeowner's phone) rather than being targeted and scoped.

title: Sensitive Data Collection
description: The homeowner's phone is accessed to receive notifications, implying personal data is collected and processed.

title: Excessive Exposure
description: Personal data is made accessible to a predetermined set of external parties (the phone) without specific consent or targeting.

title: Data Propagation
description: Aggregated device-usage analytics are propagated to the Cloud Analytics Vendor (EE3) without explicit consent or necessary scope, potentially exposing sensitive personal data beyond functional requirements.

title: Involved Parties
description: Personal device-usage analytics are shared with a dynamic set of external parties (Cloud Analytics Vendor) rather than a predetermined, static, and limited set.

title: Availability/Accessibility
description: The aggregated analytics data is made accessible to the external vendor, potentially amplifying the risk of data exposure beyond what is strictly necessary.

title: Data type sensitivity
description: The video clip data is highly sensitive and should only be collected and processed when strictly required for the video playback functionality.
assumptions: The video clip is considered personal data due to its content.

title: Data type granularity
description: The video clip data is of a fine-grained level of granularity (e.g., specific timestamps, resolution, codec) that is not functionally needed for the playback.
assumptions: The system processes metadata beyond what is strictly required for playback.

title: Treatment, analysis, enrichment, transformation
description: The video clip data is further processed, analyzed, and potentially transformed (e.g., compression, encoding) in ways that are not necessary to achieve the system's functional goal of playback.
assumptions: The system performs additional processing on the video data beyond simple storage.

title: Propagation
description: The video clip data is accessible by or propagated to other services or the mobile app backend where it is not strictly needed.
assumptions: The data is accessible to other services or the backend process.

title: Involved parties
description: Personal data (the video clip) is made accessible to more parties than functionally necessary, including the mobile app backend and potentially external services.
assumptions: The data is shared with the backend process and potentially other services.
